entries.comment: Equipment: Psychic Lasso, Psychic Grapple, Psychic Boots and the psychic Morph Ball upgrades (Viewros)
entries.content:
On Viewros (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond) Samus rebuilt her mobility with psychic counterparts of older tools, powered by the psychic crystal. Most act on Lamorn structures of compressed Psychic Energy that lie dormant until her Psychic Visor materializes them.

- Psychic Lasso: a rope of psychic energy that seizes a marked object and hauls it toward her, tearing off locks, latches and hatches and dragging away debris, much as the Grapple Lasso did during the Phazon crisis. She took it from a Psychic Container in the Tracking Operations room of the Ice Belt's bio-labs; such containers hold items Lamorn priests prepared for their prophesied Chosen One and open only to telekinesis. Atop the Chrono Tower she used it to rip away the tentacles shielding Sylux.
- Psychic Grapple: her swing line, won in Flare Pool after Phenoros died. It latches onto the Grapple Points the Lamorn built for their Maintenance Tanks, onto Psychic Grapple Points that must first be materialized, and onto Grapple Nodes, where she can reel in and hang on a sheer wall. Swinging builds momentum to carry her across wide gaps; in the Great Mines the crystal shells of Crystal Crawlers served as anchors.
- Psychic Boots: her suit lost its second jump when she arrived. The boots, recovered after Xelios fell at Volt Forge, restored a mid-air second jump, like her old Space Jump Boots, and let her stand on Psychic Platforms: condensed Psychic Energy that her visor materializes in linked groups and that no one can stand on without the boots.
- Psychic Boost Ball: dropped by Keratos in the Ice Belt. It keeps the Boost Ball's charged burst and adds Psychic Boost Rails, curving tracks along natural flows of Psychic Energy that, once materialized and entered at a boost, carry her at speed to their end.
- Psychic Spider Ball: hidden in the Ancient Temple of the Ice Belt, revealed when she set Psychic Motes into the base of a Lamorn statue. A thin film of Psychic Energy binds the ball to Psychic Ball Tracks left by Lamorn priests, across walls and ceilings, and it magnetizes to the Lamorn Magnetic Tracks built for Maintenance Tanks. With the Psychic Grapple fixed to a Tether Node, she can pull the line taut and slingshot herself.

See Psychic abilities (Viewros), The Lamorn, Grapple Beam, Boost Ball, Spider Ball and Spider Magnet, and Hi-Jump Boots, Space Jump and Wall Jump.
entries.notes: Every name and acquisition point checked against two or more independent sources. Psychic Lasso: Tracking Operations, Ice Belt, per VGC, rogue.site (Psychic Container, 'gift from the past') and VULKK; Nintendo Life lists it as 'Lasso' under Ice Belt. Psychic Grapple: Phenoros, per VGC, Gamereactor and GameSpot/game8 search snippets; Nintendo Life lists it under Flare Pool; the in-game Technology logbook (Omega Metroid transcripts) names it. Psychic Boots: Xelios, per VGC ('a second jump while airborne'), Gamereactor and a GamesRadar snippet; Nintendo Life lists it under Volt Forge; the logbook says Psychic Platforms cannot be stood on without them. Nintendo Life says Samus lost her double jump on arrival. Psychic Boost Ball: Keratos, per VGC and rogue.site (which calls it 'Psychic Ball Boost'); Nintendo Life lists it under Ice Belt; the logbook 'Psychic Boost Rail' entry names it. Psychic Spider Ball: Ancient Temple via the Ice Belt, per VGC (mote puzzle), rogue.site (motes set into the statue base), and game8/GameSpot/Digital Phablet snippets ('Ice Belt - Ancient Temple'); Nintendo Life's page omits it. Psychic Platforms: logbook, plus VGC and Omega Metroid for materializing them with the visor. Psychic Container purpose comes from the logbook. The Lasso use against Sylux is confirmed by Omega Metroid, VULKK and Nintendo Life's final-boss guide. Omitted: Gamereactor's claim that the Psychic Glove makes the platforms (VGC and Omega say the visor does); 'given by the Lamornians'; the password-glyph detail. Metroid Wiki has no pages for these items (Psychic_Boots and Fire_Shot return 404; its Prime 4 page lists only basic items), and Wikitroid was reachable only through snippets. CONSISTENCY FLAGS: (1) the Grapple Beam entry's line 'On Viewros her lock-on also helps her connect the Grapple Beam' should name the Psychic Grapple; (2) the notes on 'Equipment: Boost Ball, Spider Ball and Spider Magnet' and 'Equipment: Psychic abilities (Viewros)' saying the psychic balls could not be confirmed are now out of date.

entries.comment: Equipment: Fire, Ice and Thunder Shots and the Psychic Bombs (Viewros)
entries.content:
Samus's striking power on Viewros (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond) came from three hands: the Lamorn, the creatures she killed, and the engineer Myles MacKenzie.

Elemental shots. Myles, who writes weapons software, built three chips she salvaged from Lamorn machinery into new Arm Cannon shots at his Base Camp in Fury Green. They spend Shot Ammo.
- Fire Shot, from the Fire Chip she knocked off a scrapyard crane's plasma cutter in Flare Pool: sets targets burning, clears webs, foliage and flammable metal, melts ice and lights torches. Snow Wolves and Frostburn Grievers succumb fast to heat; gun-proof Web Crawler silk burns instantly.
- Ice Shot, from the Ice Chip in a cryopod she dropped from the Ice Belt's Loading Crane: freezes enemies in place, turns water jets and drains to ice and breaks cold locks.
- Thunder Shot, from the Thunder Chip she pried from a damaged power cell in the Volt Forge Power Core, where a Psy-bot decoy of Sylux ambushed her: energizes generators, conduits and launchers and blows open thunder locks.
The six Lamorn shrines of Sol Valley strengthened each. A charged Fire Shot looses three piercing rounds, a Super Fire Shot a long barrage that leaves enemies ablaze; the charged Ice Shot throws four bouncing balls of ice, the Super Ice Shot a wide, ricocheting flurry; the charged Thunder Shot hurls a bolt of lightning, the Super Thunder Shot a sustained arc shocking everything near its target.

Psychic Bombs. Carvex's death in Fury Green gave her the Psychic Bomb, the Morph Ball explosive of Viewros. It still bomb-jumps her and triggers Bomb Slots, and the Psychic Glove can seize a live one and hurl it at a distant slot or an enemy's feet. The Psychic Power Bomb, taken from the Omega Griever of the Great Mines, which dangled it on its tongue as bait, destroys Denzium Federation crates, crystal walls and cracked Lamorn statues and powers enhanced Bomb Slots.

Missiles and beam. In the Great Mines' Blast Mining chamber she recovered Super Missiles, which shatter blue Koornicite Ore and reinforced gate locks; their blasts draw the sound-hunting Maul Grievers. Green Energy banked at the Altar of Legacy made her Psychic Beam shots faster and stronger, then sped her steered Control Beam shots.

The elemental shots joined Lamorn hardware to Federation engineering, from the man whose "Teammates?" she had answered with a nod (see Myles MacKenzie and the stranded Federation squad).
entries.notes: Two or more independent sources for each name. Fire Chip/Fire Shot: VGC (crane's plasma cutter, Flare Pool), Inverse (Flare Pool crane; Myles at the Fury Green base camp) and rogue.site ('Scrapyard', plasma torch knocked off by a bomb). Nintendo Life files the Fire Shot under its Volt Forge section, which reflects how the guide is organized, not a location. Ice Chip/Ice Shot: VGC and rogue.site (Loading Crane cryopod, Ice Belt; Myles), plus a Wikitroid snippet (freezes enemies; opens 'Lock Unit - Cold'). Thunder Chip/Thunder Shot: VGC ('pulled from the generator after defeating Sylux') and rogue.site (broken power cell in the Volt Forge Power Core; grabbing it starts the Sylux fight). Gamereactor's 'Tower 1 electrified sublevel' was not used. The Sylux there was a Psy-bot decoy, per Omega Metroid's boss guide and the existing Prime 4 entries. Shrine variant names are confirmed by Nintendo Life, VGC and Omega Metroid. Which shrine gives which variant depends on the order they are completed (Omega notes Rings of Stone gives the Charged Fire Shot if done before Ladder of Thought; VGC and Nintendo Life/rogue disagree on Floating Path vs Source of Spring), so no shrine is mapped to a variant. Variant effects come from the Omega shrine guide and Inverse; Shot Ammo costs (3/15/5) omitted. Psychic Bomb from Carvex: VGC, GameSpot, game8, TheGamer and rogue.site. The glove throw is from Omega Metroid (shot expansion #9; boss guide) and Gamereactor ('manipulable psychic mote'). Psychic Power Bomb from the Omega Griever: VGC, Gamereactor and game8/VULKK snippets; Nintendo Life lists it under Great Mines. The bait detail is from the Omega boss guide plus a search-result guide; targets (Denzium crates, crystal walls, cracked statues, enhanced Bomb Slots) are from Omega. Super Missile: VGC and Omega (Blast Mining); Nintendo Life and Gamereactor list it under Great Mines. Koornicite, gate locks and drawing Grievers are from Omega, consistent with the Grievers entry's 'loud noises draw hordes'. Heat weaknesses and Web Crawler silk come from in-game Biology logbook transcripts. Altar rewards (25%: stronger Psychic Beam; 50%: faster Control shot) are from Omega and Gamereactor; Nintendo Life names them 'Psychic Beam Upgrade' and 'Control Beam Boost'. Omitted as single-source: Varmis killed by a Power Bomb detonated inside it, the Psychic Power Bomb's 3-round capacity, Psychic Bombs thrown to break the decoy Sylux's tornado, and Keratos's ice wall melted by the Fire Shot. Keys: 'Super Fire Shot', 'Charged Ice Shot' and similar are already caught by the base shot keys under whole-word matching, so slots went to the chips, the Power Bomb plural and Shot Ammo.

entries.comment: Equipment: Other M combat techniques: Sense Move, Overblast, Lethal Strike, Concentration and Accel Charge
entries.content:
Aboard the Bottle Ship (Metroid: Other M) Samus fought in a fast, acrobatic close-quarters style built on five techniques.

Sense Move (SenseMove). An instant before an attack lands she hops or flips forward, backward or sideways, and the blow meets empty air. If she triggers it while charging, her beam reaches full charge almost at once, so every dodge becomes a counterattack. A Galactic Federation scientist taught it to her after her last mission on Zebes (Super Metroid); in the training exercise she first used it to dodge laser fire from a holographic Zebesian ("OK, looking good. Let's check your reaction time. Here come some beams—dodge 'em."). It was no luxury: the Brug Mass could not be hurt until she had dodged it.

Overblast. She leaps onto an enemy, usually one already knocked down, lands on its head or another vulnerable spot and, as her beam charges by itself, fires point-blank before springing clear, throwing the target back or flattening it. If she hesitates, the creature throws her off. One Overblast kills a Sidehopper outright, it works against larger foes such as Goyagma, and she can chain it from creature to creature without touching the ground. Kyratians of the Cryosphere are recorded as capable of it too.

Lethal Strike. When a large enemy such as a Zebesian is down, she closes in, builds a full charge and drives it into the creature's vulnerable spot, usually killing it outright.

Concentration. Standing still and uninterrupted, she focuses until her Missiles are fully restocked; in an emergency, with her energy low enough, it also restores part of her Energy, more slowly. Three E-Recovery Tanks found aboard let her begin concentrating sooner and recover one more Energy Tank's worth each.

Accel Charge. Six small, yellow, glowing capsules hidden aboard each quickened her charge, for both the Charge Beam, which also loads her Super Missiles, and her Power Bombs; with all six it filled in under a second.

In a fight, Samus is no stationary gunner. She reads the tell, slips the attack at the last instant with her cannon already charging, answers at point-blank range, vaults onto a staggered enemy to fire into its head, and ends a downed foe with one charged strike; between clashes she stands still to concentrate and restock. See Melee Counter and Omega Cannon, Charge Beam and Charge Combos, and The Bottle Ship incident.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki spells it 'Sensemove (also written Sense Move)'. Wikipedia writes 'Sense Move'; SenseMove is kept as an alias. The training story and the scientist's quote are verbatim from Metroid Wiki's Sense Move page; the Brug Mass detail is from the same page; 'hop, flip' follows the official-site quote cited there. The Overblast mechanics (lands on head, automatic charge, thrown off if slow, chaining, one-hit Sidehoppers, effective against Goyagma) are from Metroid Wiki, and Wikipedia confirms the point-blank charged shot. The Kyratian claim rests only on the Metroid Wiki Overblast infobox listing Kyratians as users, with no detail. A Wikitroid snippet that a Kyratian kicks Samus off was not used, and 'of the Cryosphere' comes from search snippets of the Kyratian page (Metroid Wiki has no Kyratian page). Metroid Wiki names Zebesians, the Brug Mass and Phantoon as Lethal Strike targets; only the Zebesian is kept, to respect the one-clause limit on the Brug Mass. Concentration: per Metroid Wiki and the manual, E-Recovery Tanks raise the energy threshold below which Concentration restores Energy, which the entry renders as 'begin concentrating sooner'. Three tanks, each adding one Energy Tank's worth (Metroid Wiki). Accel Charge: six capsules; it speeds both the Charge Beam (and Super Missile) charge and the Power Bomb charge; with all six the meter fills in under a second (Metroid Wiki). Locations omitted. Metroid Wiki's line that Concentration 'replaced the energy units of previous games' was dropped as meta. Bare 'Concentration' was not used as a key because it is a common English word. Does not repeat the Melee Counter, Charge Beam basics, Adam's authorization system or the incident narrative.

result.research_notes: The audit's verification problem is solved by in-game text. Omega Metroid's Logbook Guide: Technology gives verbatim in-game scan transcripts that name the Psychic Platform, Psychic Grapple (with Grapple Points, Psychic Grapple Points and Grapple Nodes), Psychic Spider Ball (Psychic Ball Tracks, Lamorn Magnetic Tracks, Tether Nodes), Psychic Boost Ball (Psychic Boost Rails) and Psychic Boots. Its Psychic Container transcript says the Lamorn priests prepared items for the Chosen One. Acquisition points were cross-checked between the VGC walkthrough and Nintendo Life's power-suit upgrade list, the two sources the critic named, plus rogue.site, Inverse, Gamereactor and several search snippets (GameSpot, game8, GamesRadar, VULKK, TheGamer, Digital Phablet). Discrepancies resolved: (1) the Psychic Spider Ball is in the Ice Belt's Ancient Temple per VGC, rogue, game8, GameSpot and Digital Phablet, though Nintendo Life omits it; (2) Fire Chip in Flare Pool per VGC, Inverse and rogue; (3) the Thunder Chip is in the Volt Forge Power Core, guarded by a Sylux decoy, per VGC and rogue; (4) the shrine-to-variant mapping depends on the order shrines are completed, so it was left out. Nothing named in the brief had to be omitted. Metroid Wiki has no pages for the Prime 4 items (404s), and its Prime 4 article lists only basic gear. Other M techniques rest on Metroid Wiki's pages (Sense Move, Overblast, Lethal Strike, Concentration, Accel Charge, E-Recovery Tank) with Wikipedia corroboration. Kyratian has no Metroid Wiki page and the breezewiki mirror of Wikitroid was blocked. GameSpot gallery and game8 pages returned 403 or empty to WebFetch and were used only through search snippets. Consistency flags for the merge pass: the Grapple Beam entry's Viewros line should name the Psychic Grapple, and the notes on the Boost/Spider Ball and Psychic abilities entries saying the psychic balls were unconfirmed are now out of date. All three entries are 395-400 words and each uses one game title in parentheses (the Other M entry uses two).
